notes: §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR9: no pair of the SORT's file-names in one SAME SORT AREA or SAME SORT-MERGE AREA clause, and "File-names associated with the GIVING phrase may not be specified in the same SAME clause", which at 85 reaches "SAME RECORD AREA FOR file-name" ... as well as SAME AREA (§1985:VII.2.13.2). FileControlBinder.BindIoControl records each SAME clause on FileModel.SameClauses and SortBindFile calls SortBinder.ScreenSameClauses, which refuses a pair of the statement's files (file-name-1 included) in a sort or sort-merge area clause, two GIVING files in a SAME AREA clause, and, below 2002 (held1985, kb/Work PB5276, landed), two GIVING files in a SAME RECORD AREA clause; MERGE keeps its own arm. Probes at --std 85 (work-rs-02/c9; SORT SW USING IN1 IN2 GIVING OUT1 OUT2): (b) refused COBOL1757: SAME SORT AREA FOR SW IN1, SAME SORT-MERGE AREA FOR SW OUT2, SAME SORT AREA FOR SW2 IN1 IN2, SAME AREA FOR OUT1 OUT2, SAME RECORD AREA FOR OUT1 OUT2 and FOR OUT1 IN1 OUT2; accepted and run ('AAAA', 'BBBB', 'CCCC'): SAME SORT AREA FOR SW2 IN1, FOR SW SW2, SAME RECORD AREA FOR IN1 OUT1, FOR IN1 IN2 OUT2, FOR SW OUT1, SAME AREA FOR IN1 IN2; (c) at --std 2023 SAME RECORD AREA FOR OUT1 OUT2 compiles and runs and SAME AREA FOR OUT1 OUT2 is still refused. Classes a, d, e and f do not reach a file-name pairing rule. Witness: SAME SORT AREA and SAME SORT-MERGE AREA pairs, refused. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5276 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5276 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-02.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-02-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "File-names associated with the GIVING phrase may not be specified in the same SAME clause."; 2023: "File-names associated with the GIVING phrase shall not be specified in the same SAME AREA clause.". First sentence matches. 1985 bars GIVING files from sharing any SAME clause; 2023 bars only SAME AREA, so sharing a SAME RECORD AREA clause is no longer refused.
